analysis.investment_thesis: Neptune Logitek fails the Magic Formula's "good business" test decisively — a 0.51% ROE implies near-zero return on capital, making the 9.24x P/E a classic value trap rather than a bargain. The Magic Formula requires BOTH cheapness and quality; this has only a whiff of the former.
key_strengths: P/E of 9.24 is optically cheap versus Indian market averages
Exposure to structurally growing Indian logistics sector
key_risks: ROE of 0.51% signals catastrophically low return on capital — fails Magic Formula quality screen
Tiny INR 66 Cr market cap — illiquid, likely asset-light broker with no moat
No disclosed EBIT/EV or ROIC data to verify earnings yield rigorously
red_flags: Low-margin logistics broker competing against giants (Delhivery, Allcargo, TCI)
Recent BSE listing with limited operating history visible
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Magic Formula lens, this is a near-automatic reject. Return on capital is the single most important quality filter I use, and a 0.51% ROE is a red siren — even with modest leverage, ROIC is almost certainly in the low single digits, well below my 20%+ threshold for a "good" business. The P/E of 9.24 suggests a ~10.8% earnings yield, which is decent but not compelling enough to compensate for a business that earns essentially nothing on its capital base. Cheap garbage remains garbage; the Magic Formula explicitly requires BOTH legs.

Indian logistics is a growth industry, but it's a brutal, fragmented, low-margin business where scale wins. A 66 Cr micro-cap without demonstrated capital efficiency is unlikely to compound shareholder wealth — every rupee reinvested returns roughly nothing. I'd pass entirely and redeploy capital to Indian names that rank well on BOTH earnings yield and ROIC.
